subject: Hosted API: commit uplift & rate-lane rework — Appcart renewal
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@appcart.com>, Elena Morrison <elena@appcart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-31T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API: commit uplift & rate-lane rework — Appcart renewal

Samir / Elena —

Thanks for the time last week. Per our renewal playbook and your growth pattern, attached is a proposal that combines a higher committed monthly token band with a softened rate-lane for burst traffic so you can avoid hard throttles during peak campaigns. High-level: (attached PDF)

- Monthly committed band: 1.5M tokens -> 3.0M tokens (step-up over first 60 days)
- Rate lanes: new mid-tier at 0.9x standard price for additional headroom before burst pricing
- Soft-throttle behavior: gradual degradation with model-fallback to a compatible, lower-cost variant once soft-threshold exceeded
- Proposed term: 12 months, annual billing with a 30-day onboarding credit for engineering time

Could you review the attached and confirm whether Appcart procurement needs a PO-first workflow or DocuSign? If PO, we can stage an invoice draft and give you a billing window.

I've looped in Kimberly for pricing approvals and Vanessa for ops/CS handoff. If you want, we can run a short canary of the new rate-lane for 14 days after sign to validate latency and cost.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm procurement path (DocuSign vs PO)
2) Sign proposal or request changes — we can incorporate a retention clause if you prefer multi-term credits
3) Ops kickoff with Vanessa to map burst windows and fallback cadence

Thanks —

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Redwood_Appcart_Proposal_20270831.pdf

From: Samir Patel <samir@appcart.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morrison <elena@appcart.com>
Date: 2027-08-31T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: commit uplift & rate-lane rework — Appcart renewal

Lauren —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the summary. A few quick questions before we loop procurement:

1) The step-up from 1.5M to 3.0M over 60 days — will usage above 1.5M in month 1 be pro-rated at the new mid-tier, or will it bill as overage until the step completes? We need to understand month-to-month cash flows.
2) On soft-throttle and model-fallback — can you confirm which model variant will be used for fallback and whether embeddings/semantic-search latency is covered under the same SLO?
3) What are the invoice timing options? We typically do net-30 on an annual invoice but can do prepaid credits if there's a discount.

Procurement prefers PO-first but if DocuSign is faster we can circulate an internal exception. Elena — any blocking items from your side?

Thanks,
Samir
VP Product, Appcart Inc
samir@appcart.com

Date: 2027-09-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: commit uplift & rate-lane rework — Appcart renewal

Samir —

Great questions. Quick answers:

1) Step-up billing: we will pro-rate usage above 1.5M in month 1 at the mid-tier rate (0.9x) for any volume between 1.5M and 3.0M while the step-up completes. Overage only applies if you exceed the 3.0M cap during a monthly cycle. We'll call this out in section 3.2 of the attached SOW.

2) Fallback model: we'll route to "redwood-lite-1.1" (same embedding family) for degradation. Embeddings and semantic search requests routed to the fallback will have separate latency SLOs (documented in the ops annex) — typically 20-30% higher p95 but with cost savings. Vanessa has the annex ready to share.

3) Invoice timing: we support PO-first net-30, prepaid annual credits (2.5% discount), or upfront annual prepay (4% discount). If procurement needs a PO, send an initial PO against the proposal and we'll generate an invoice draft.

I'll attach a revised SOW that clarifies the billing behavior and fallback ops.

Lauren

Attachments: Appcart_SOW_revised_20270901.docx

Hi Samir / team —

Following up with operational detail so your engineering team can plan the canary and fallback behavior. High level:

- Canary window: 14 days after contract effective date, scoped to 10% traffic sampled by token distribution. We’ll provide a shortterm observability dashboard with token-level latencies and cost delta.
- Fallback policy: requests that exceed the soft-threshold will be tagged and routed to redwood-lite-1.1; we keep a KV cache on the primary model so the fallback hit rate should be minimal.
- Rate-lane smoothing: mid-tier capacity will be subject to a 10-minute continuous-window throttling policy to avoid burst storms; you can request emergency burst credits via the console for unexpected spikes.

I've attached a small ops annex to the SOW that includes the p95/p99 targets and runbook excerpts. If Appcart engineering wants to validate locally, I can share a sandbox endpoint and a short load script.

Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success — Onboarding
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: Appcart_SOW_revised_20270901.docx

Lauren / Vanessa / Kimberly —

Thanks for the proposal and the updated SOW. Procurement has reviewed and we can proceed PO-first. Attached is a draft PO referencing DEAL-4532. A couple of housekeeping items:

- Please confirm final billing contact and remit-to details for the invoice (we use Net-30).
- We will need a final signed SOW attached to the PO — happy to accept a DocuSign link if you prefer that route.
- We're requesting the initial invoice to be dated for the contract effective date of 2027-09-15 and to include the 60-day step-up schedule as a line item.

If you can send the DocuSign envelope for the SOW + proposal, we'll circulate internally and return a signed PO within 3 business days.

Procurement Team
Appcart Inc
